_readme: Hand-maintained. One entry per dataset deliberately exempted from the tier-1 registry-coverage fence, each with a reason a reviewer can judge. Keep this file SMALL — its sibling contracts/api_response_exceptions.json holds three entries after months of use. If this list is growing, the predicate is wrong, not the datasets. SHAPE: scripts/dataset_inventory.py::_exceptions() reads the `allowed` LIST — each entry {table, findings[], reason}. A key by any other name is read by nothing; `allowed_unwatched` sat here as an empty object that no code has ever loaded.

allowed.reason: Capacity Source listings are watched PER LISTING, by routes/exclusive_listings._freshness(), not by a whole-table freshness registry — and neither registry can express that rule without inverting its own meaning. THREE measured reasons, each read out of the code: (1) BOTH REGISTRIES SCAN WHOLE TABLES WITH NO PREDICATE. data_freshness_radar._max_ts_and_count runs `MAX(<col>) FROM <table>` and infra_growth._LAYERS is the same (label, table, category, stale_days) shape. Liveness here is routes.exclusive_listings._LIVE_WHERE (status public or pocket, not past expires_at). A withdrawn or expired listing keeps its updated_at, so a whole-table MAX would read `fresh` off exactly the rows the product must NOT publish — a false GREEN over a sitemap carrying nothing. (2) DORMANT AT ZERO IS A FALSE ALARM. Capacity Source is deliberately dormant at zero live listings (the owner removes the sample listings after a meeting). With the table empty, _max_ts_and_count returns ts_used=None, _classify returns `unknown`, and the detail string is "table 'exclusive_listings' present but no usable timestamp column" — which contains "no usable timestamp", the exact substring dchub_self_heal.fix_data_freshness_radar matches to escalate `data_source_missing` into actionable_backend_issues. Registering the table would page a human every heal pull for a state the owner chose. (3) THE THRESHOLD IS PER-ROW, NOT PER-TABLE. Both registries hold ONE scalar per entry (sla_hours / stale_days). The real rule is _CADENCE_OVERDUE_DAYS = {real_time: 2, weekly: 9, monthly: 35} applied to each listing's own verification.verified_at, which _freshness() already computes and every teaser already publishes as freshness.overdue with next_update_due. WHAT WOULD RETIRE THIS EXCEPTION: a registry entry that accepts (a) a row predicate so it measures only live rows, (b) a zero-row disposition of `dormant` that does not escalate, and (c) a per-row staleness rule instead of one scalar. Any one of the three alone is not enough — (a) without (b) turns the dormant state into a permanent breach. Pinned by tests/test_listings_freshness_is_watched_per_listing.py, which fails if the per-listing rule or the dormant behaviour goes away.

A URL routing map, not a dataset with a freshness. util/frozen_slug.py (backend#5611) reads it only to turn an OLD facility slug into its canonical slug, one hop, so /api/v1/facility/<slug> (MCP fetch/get_facility) finds the same building the profile page already finds. No field of it is published: the response is the facility row, whose own tables are watched. Rows are written once by routes/facility_slug_freeze.py when a slug changes and are correct forever after, so a MAX(created_at) age says nothing about staleness; an empty or old table is the healthy state. The page route (routes/facility_profile_page.py) has read it since 2026-07-03 without being flagged because it is not MCP-served.
